E-Commerce Customer Purchase Prediction — Logistic Regression¶

Company: ShopSmart | Domain: E-Commerce | Task: Binary classification (0 = No Purchase, 1 = Purchase) | Sapphire IQ ML Project

Workflow: 1) Load & understand data → 2) EDA → 3) Preprocessing (missing values, outliers, encoding, scaling) → 4) Logistic Regression → 5) Evaluation → 6) Predict for new customers → 7) Business insights

3. Preprocessing¶

To avoid data leakage, the data is split first (80/20, stratified) and every statistic (imputation values, outlier caps, scaling) is learned from the training set only.

  • Missing values: median for numeric, mode for categorical
  • Outliers: IQR winsorising (cap at Q1−1.5·IQR / Q3+1.5·IQR) on continuous columns — values are capped, not dropped, so no customers are lost
  • Encoding: one-hot (drop first) for the 5 categorical columns
  • Scaling: StandardScaler
In [9]:
X = df.drop(columns=['Customer_ID','Purchase']); y = df.Purchase
Xtr,Xte,ytr,yte = train_test_split(X,y,test_size=0.2,stratify=y,random_state=RS)
print(Xtr.shape, Xte.shape)

class IQRCapper(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    def __init__(self,k=1.5): self.k=k
    def fit(self,X,y=None):
        X=pd.DataFrame(X); q1,q3=X.quantile(.25),X.quantile(.75); i=q3-q1
        self.lo_,self.hi_=(q1-self.k*i).values,(q3+self.k*i).values; return self
    def transform(self,X): return np.clip(np.asarray(X,float),self.lo_,self.hi_)
    def get_feature_names_out(self,names=None): return np.asarray(names)

cont = ['Age','Session_Duration_Min','Pages_Viewed','Cart_Value_INR','Discount_Percent','Days_Since_Last_Visit']
disc = ['Products_Viewed','Cart_Items','Previous_Orders','Email_Open_Rate','Customer_Rating','Returns_Last_Year']
# how many values get capped (train)
q1,q3=Xtr[cont].quantile(.25),Xtr[cont].quantile(.75); iqr=q3-q1
print(((Xtr[cont]<q1-1.5*iqr)|(Xtr[cont]>q3+1.5*iqr)).sum().rename('outliers capped (train)'))

pre = ColumnTransformer([
    ('cont',Pipeline([('imp',SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),('cap',IQRCapper()),('sc',StandardScaler())]),cont),
    ('disc',Pipeline([('imp',SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),('sc',StandardScaler())]),disc),
    ('cat',Pipeline([('imp',SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')),('oh',OneHotEncoder(drop='first',handle_unknown='ignore'))]),cat)])
pre.fit(Xtr)
names = pre.get_feature_names_out()
Xtr_p = pd.DataFrame(pre.transform(Xtr),columns=names); print(Xtr_p.shape, 'missing after:', Xtr_p.isna().sum().sum())

# Cleaned full dataset (for reference/sharing) - same steps, fitted on all data
clean = X.copy()
clean[num] = SimpleImputer(strategy='median').fit_transform(X[num])
clean[cat] = SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent').fit_transform(X[cat])
for c in cont:
    q1,q3=clean[c].quantile(.25),clean[c].quantile(.75); i=q3-q1; clean[c]=clean[c].clip(q1-1.5*i,q3+1.5*i)
clean.insert(0,'Customer_ID',df.Customer_ID); clean['Purchase']=y
clean.round(4).to_csv('outputs/Ecommerce_Purchase_Cleaned.csv',index=False)

4. Logistic Regression model¶

In [11]:
model = Pipeline([('pre',pre),('clf',LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000,random_state=RS))])
model.fit(Xtr,ytr)
ypred = model.predict(Xte); yprob = model.predict_proba(Xte)[:,1]
cv = cross_val_score(model,Xtr,ytr,cv=StratifiedKFold(5,shuffle=True,random_state=RS),scoring='roc_auc')
print('5-fold CV ROC-AUC (train): %.4f +/- %.4f'%(cv.mean(),cv.std()))

5-fold CV ROC-AUC (train): 0.7281 +/- 0.0071

Optional check: threshold tuning¶

The default cut-off is 0.5. Because the classes are imbalanced (≈65% purchasers) the table below shows the trade-off if marketing prefers catching more non-buyers or more buyers.

7. Conclusions¶

Test metrics: {'Accuracy': 0.704, 'Precision': 0.728, 'Recall': 0.869, 'F1-score': 0.792, 'ROC-AUC': 0.741}

                    feature  coefficient  odds_ratio

Traffic_Source_Social Media       -0.350       0.705

Key takeaways

  • Cart_Items is the strongest purchase driver (odds ratio ≈ 1.84 per +1 SD), followed by Premium membership (≈ 1.7× vs. New members) and Cart_Value_INR (≈ 1.5×). Session duration, pages viewed and products viewed add smaller positive effects.
  • Visitors from Email (the baseline traffic source) convert best; Social Media, Organic, Referral and Paid Ads traffic all have lower odds (≈ 0.70–0.77×).
  • Returns last year and long gaps since the last visit lower purchase likelihood slightly.
  • Marketing actions: target customers with filled/high-value carts (cart-recovery messages), push Premium/loyalty offers, invest in email campaigns, and re-engage lapsed visitors.
  • Caveat: ROC-AUC ≈ 0.74 means moderate predictive power. The model has high recall (it finds most buyers) but lower specificity; use the probabilities to rank and target customers, and tune the threshold to the campaign's cost trade-off.
